tool.name: cors_deep_check
tool.description:
Probe a URL for CORS misconfiguration laxity. Goes beyond the static `Origin: <attacker>` reflection check in `http_security_headers_audit` (#47) by probing 10 origin-bypass classes plus pre-flight method/header laxity:
**Origin probes (GET with attacker-controlled `Origin: ...` request header)**: - `null_origin` — `Origin: null` (sandboxed iframes / `data:` URIs). - `baseline_evil` — direct attacker host `https://strix-<nonce>.evil.example`. - `subdomain_suffix` — `https://strix.evil.<target>` (catches `endswith` validators). - `subdomain_prefix` — `https://<target>.evil.example` (catches `startswith` / unanchored regex). - `subdomain_substring` — `https://<target>-evil.example` (catches substring). - `trailing_slash` — `https://<target>/` (catches bare-host allow-list mismatch). - `scheme_swap` — `http://<target>` (catches https-only allow-list bypassed via http). - `userinfo_confusion` — `https://<target>@evil.example` (catches misparsed netloc). - `backslash_bypass` — `https://<target>\.evil.example`. - `backtick_bypass` — `https://<target>` + backtick + `.evil.example`.
For each probe, server reflects `Origin` into `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` → finding. With `Allow-Credentials: true` → **critical** CWE-942 (full credentialed bypass). Without credentials → **high**. `null` reflection with credentials → **high**. Wildcard + credentials → **high** (browsers reject this combo, but it documents intent).
**Pre-flight method laxity** (OPTIONS with `Access-Control-Request-Method: TRACE / DELETE / CONNECT`): server echoes the method into `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` → **medium** CWE-942 (no method validation).
**Pre-flight header laxity** (OPTIONS with `Access-Control-Request-Headers: X-Bogus-... / X-Internal-User-Id`): server echoes the header name into `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` → **medium** CWE-942 (no header validation; attacker can send framework-internal headers cross-origin).
Per-(severity, issue) dedup so a single broken validator doesn't cascade into 5 near-identical findings.
Skip cases: - Baseline GET non-2xx/3xx → origin probes skip; pre-flight probes still run (they don't depend on a 2xx baseline). - `--exclude-path` blocks the URL → graceful no-op.
**Safety**: - Read-only (GET + OPTIONS only, no follow-redirects, no body). - Attacker host gets a unique random `strix-<nonce>.evil.example` prefix per run for log auditability. - Composes with cluster-A safety (`--exclude-path` / `--rate-limit` / `--auth-*`). - Severity-tailored `description_plain` + `recommended_action` (replace dynamic Origin reflection with explicit allow-list of trusted origins; reject `null` Origins; never set Allow-Credentials alongside reflected/wildcard origins; explicitly list intended methods/headers in pre-flight responses) and `verification_status=needs_review` since reflection alone doesn't always equal exploitable in the customer's threat model.

parameter.name: target_url
parameter.description: URL to probe. Bare hostnames are auto-prefixed with `https://`. Examples: `https://api.example.com/v1/profile`, `https://app.example.com/api/users`. The probe sends GETs with attacker-controlled `Origin` headers and OPTIONS pre-flight requests.

returns.description:
{success, target_url, target_host, baseline: {status, body_length, error?, skipped?}, origin_probes: [{label, probe_origin, reflected, credentialed, wildcard, severity, issue, evidence, aco_header, acc_header}, ...], preflight_probes: [{label, request_method, request_header, response_methods, response_headers, echoed, severity, evidence}, ...], findings_emitted}.
The agent should follow up critical-severity findings by manually constructing a victim-side proof-of-concept fetch from the bypassing origin to confirm the cookies / Authorization header are actually attached.
